title: Shot Twice. He Never Dropped the Flag.

brand.cta: Follow The Black History Room for one story a day.

beats.text: Shot twice. He never dropped the flag.

overlays.hook: Shot twice. *He never dropped the flag.*

beats.text: Born enslaved in Norfolk, Virginia, in 1840, he found freedom up north, in New Bedford, Massachusetts.
In 1863, when Black men were finally allowed to fight, he joined the 54th Massachusetts.
On July 18, 1863, the 54th charged Fort Wagner, near Charleston.

visual.caption: The charge of the 54th Massachusetts at Fort Wagner, Currier & Ives, 1863

beats.text: The color sergeant was shot down. Carney grabbed the flag and carried it to the top of the wall.
He was severely wounded, twice. When the regiment fell back, he brought the flag back with it.
He told the men: Boys, I only did my duty. The old flag never touched the ground.
Discharged in 1864, he went home and delivered the mail.
The army took 37 years. In 1900, he received the Medal of Honor, for the earliest action by any Black soldier honored.

visual.caption: Sgt. William Carney wearing his Medal of Honor, c. 1900

beats.text: He died in 1908. At the Massachusetts State House, the flag flew at half-mast.
Shot twice. William Carney never dropped the flag.

facts.claim: Born enslaved in Norfolk, Virginia, 29 Feb 1840; freedom in New Bedford, Massachusetts (sources differ on how: Underground Railroad, or his father buying the family's freedom).
Joined the 54th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry in 1863 after Black men were allowed to enlist.
Assault on Fort Wagner, Morris Island near Charleston, 18 July 1863.
When the color sergeant was shot, Carney took the flag and planted it on the parapet.
Medal of Honor citation: brought off the flag 'under a fierce fire in which he was twice severely wounded'.
'Boys, I only did my duty; the old flag never touched the ground!' (as reported).
Discharged June 1864; letter carrier in New Bedford (32 years per Wikipedia).
Medal of Honor issued 23 May 1900, 37 years after the battle; the earliest action for which a Black soldier received the medal.
Died 9 Dec 1908; the flag at the Massachusetts State House flew at half-mast.

notUsed: The elevator accident at the State House as cause of death (Wikipedia and a forum only)
Wounds in the leg, chest and arm (Wikipedia only); the citation says 'twice severely wounded'
'First Black Medal of Honor recipient': wrong, 20 Black men received it before him; his was the earliest action
32 years as a mail carrier (Wikipedia only)
